status.en: 112 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Islamabad, Peshawar and Balochistan.
status.nb: 112 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Islamabad, Peshawar og Belutsjistan.

summary.en: Militant attacks continue across Pakistan, with a blast killing three children in a gas cylinder explosion in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and a shop roof collapse killing one and injuring six in Karachi. Baloch insurgent groups claim to have killed 40 Pakistani soldiers in 25 operations in Balochistan and to have killed seven soldiers in an attack involving women fighters, while security forces reported killing four terrorists in a Bajaur operation. Separate incidents include the killing of a Pakistani journalist in Karachi and the death of an Afghan woman among dozens deported, reflecting heightened security and humanitarian pressures. The conflict caused 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Militantangrep fortsetter over hele Pakistan, med en eksplosjon som drepte tre barn i en gassylinder i Khyber Pakhtunkhwa og et tak som kollapset i en butikk og drepte én og såret seks i Karachi. Balochiske opprørsgrupper hevder å ha drept 40 pakistanske soldater i 25 operasjoner i Balochistan og å ha drept syv soldater i et angrep med kvinnelige krigere, mens sikkerhetsstyrker rapporterte å ha drept fire terrorister i en operasjon i Bajaur. Separate hendelser inkluderer drapet på en pakistansk journalist i Karachi og døden til en afghansk kvinne blant dusinvis som ble deportert, noe som reflekterer økt sikkerhets- og humanitært press. Konflikten forårsaket 1 794 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
